newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Bolger gets conditional support for APEC trip.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Bolger gets conditional support for APEC trip.

text.p: New Zealand caretaker Prime Minister Jim Bolger on Tuesday won conditional support from the nationalist New Zealand First party to attend this month's APEC leaders' forum in the Philippines.

Labour leader Helen Clark and New Zealand First leader Winston Peters have been critical of the lack of consultation between the caretaker National party administration and other parties over Bolger's plan to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum on November 25.

But in a statement issued after his fifth session of coalition talks with National, New Zealand First leader Winston Peters said: "New Zealand First supports the attendance of whichever Prime Minister and ministers are holding office at the time of upcoming international meetings at which New Zealand is expected to be represented."
Peters said it was important to convey stablility to the international community and there could only be one official government at any time.
The current coalition talks are expected to take several more weeks, making it likely Bolger will attend the forum.
Labour leader Helen Clark said she had spoken to Deputy Prime Minister Don McKinnon on the question of who should attend APEC, but implied no agreement had been reached.
"I have spoken to Mr McKinnon about it," Clark said as she headed into coalition talks with New Zealand First. Asked if she was happy with the arrangement, Clark said: "What arrangement?"

Peters also cited the Food and Agriculture organisation's world food summit in Rome on November 13-17 and the Australian and New Zealand transport ministers' meeting in Australia on November 15 as other meetings ministers are expected to attend.

Tuesday's talks between Labour and New Zealand were the fifth formal session since New Zealand First emerged with the balance of power from the October 12 election. It is negotiating with both National and Labour over the shape of the next government.
Clark said she had not yet received a report on rises in state house rentals she and Peters had requested from the government.
She would give no indication of the topics to be covered in Tuesday's talks.
